# temps_feature_flag_environment (Resource)

A feature flag's value, kill switch and targeting rules in one environment. Destroying it removes the override (and the rules it manages), so the environment serves the flag default again with the switch on.

Import with `<project_id>/<key>/<environment_id>`.

Required API key permissions: `flags:read`, `flags:write`, `flags:delete`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Turn the redesigned checkout on in staging only.
resource "temps_feature_flag_environment" "new_checkout_staging" {
  project_id     = temps_project.web.id
  key            = temps_feature_flag.new_checkout.key
  environment_id = temps_environment.staging.id
  value          = jsonencode(true)
}

# In production, serve it to half of the paying customers and to the team.
resource "temps_feature_flag_environment" "new_checkout_production" {
  project_id     = temps_project.web.id
  key            = temps_feature_flag.new_checkout.key
  environment_id = temps_environment.production.id
  value          = jsonencode(false)

  rules = [
    {
      description = "Team"
      conditions  = [{ attribute = "email", operator = "matches", value = jsonencode(".*@example\\.com$") }]
      serve_value = jsonencode(true)
    },
    {
      description        = "Paying customers"
      conditions         = [{ attribute = "plan", operator = "in", value = jsonencode(["pro", "team"]) }]
      rollout_percentage = 50
      serve_value        = jsonencode(true)
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (Number) ID of an environment of `project_id`.
- `key` (String) Key of the flag, usually `temps_feature_flag.<name>.key`.
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Kill switch. `false` serves the flag default in this environment whatever `value` says. Defaults to `true`.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered targeting rules; the first rule whose conditions hold (and whose rollout includes the subject) decides the value, after the kill switch and before `value`. Left out, Terraform does not manage the rules and leaves them as they are; `rules = []` removes them all. Removing the argument stops managing them without changing them. Destroying the resource removes rules it managed. Read back from `GET /projects/{id}/flags/{key}` while set. Each rule serves exactly one of `serve_value`, `serve_variant` and `serve_split`; variants must be declared on the flag. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded value for this environment, for example `jsonencode(true)`; it must match the flag's type. Omit it to serve the flag default.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<key>/<environment_id>`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Optional:

- `conditions` (Attributes List) Conditions that must all hold. Left out, the rule matches every subject. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--conditions))
- `description` (String) Free text shown in the console, for example `Beta customers`.
- `rollout_percentage` (Number) Share of matching subjects the rule applies to (0–100); all of them when left out.
- `serve_split` (Attributes List) Split subjects across variants of the flag by weight; the weights add up to 100. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--serve_split))
- `serve_value` (String) Serve this JSON value, for example `jsonencode(true)`; it must match the flag's type.
- `serve_variant` (String) Serve this variant of the flag.

<a id="nestedatt--rules--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.conditions`

Required:

- `attribute` (String) Evaluation context attribute, for example `plan`, `country` or `email`.
- `operator` (String) One of `eq`, `neq`, `in`, `not_in`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `matches`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `exists`, `not_exists`.

Optional:

- `value` (String) JSON operand: a scalar such as `jsonencode("pro")`, a list for `in` and `not_in` (`jsonencode(["de", "fr"])`), a number for `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`. Leave it out for `exists` and `not_exists`.


<a id="nestedatt--rules--serve_split"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.serve_split`

Required:

- `variant` (String) Variant key.
- `weight` (Number) Share of the rule's subjects, in whole percent.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import temps_feature_flag_environment.new_checkout_staging 3/new-checkout/5
```
